title: Project implementation plan
scope: Build a reliable meeting-assistant evaluation, establish what its history supports, compare reactive and background reasoning, then add tools and learn when to act.
current_state: The broad bank contains 105 distinct questions across 26 conversations. A twenty-question subset is frozen across six meetings, with a separate meeting/speaker split from earlier F5 development. Current exports include the spoken Assistant cue and question audio; independent reliability review, silence controls, history retention and the four system conditions remain unfinished.
choices: Use a separate meeting assistant and an existing participant as the requester.
Freeze the existing F5-TTS checkpoint and inference recipe; do not tune the model on the evaluation meetings or speakers.
Start with pause and resume. Reference-answer audio stays deferred; score against short source-verified fact checklists.
Background preparation must not see the future question or its scoring labels.
Count the entire preparation cost, including work that is cancelled or never becomes useful.
next: Review the frozen twenty-question subset and its source fact checklists, add ordinary-discussion silence controls, and obtain human naturalness/voice ratings.
Finish matched transcript-history controls and maintain an explicit meeting state before using teacher traces as training targets.
Qualify bounded history retention, then run the original three audio questions through the four controlled conditions below.
meeting_state_schema: speaker · fact/commitment · proposed/agreed/superseded · evidence · source time

conditions.history: Audio history accessible to the speech system; no S2 reasoning.

conditions.condition: Reactive S2 with oracle transcript history
conditions.history: Ground-truth transcript history available before the request.
conditions.establishes: Reasoning ability when context is reliable.

conditions.condition: Reactive S2 with causally available ASR history
conditions.history: Only ASR output actually available by each point in the recording.
conditions.establishes: The cost of perception errors and ASR delay.

conditions.condition: Background preparation with the same ASR history
conditions.history: The identical causal ASR history; no future question or scoring facts.
conditions.establishes: Whether preparation before the request helps, including its full compute cost.

stages.title: 1. Build a small, reliable evaluation set
stages.goal: Freeze about twenty reviewed questions across four to six meetings, covering commitments, revised decisions and constraints across speakers.

tasks.text: Keep the broad reviewed question bank and its source evidence.
tasks.evidence: 105 distinct questions are available across all four retained studies; this larger inventory is not itself the small evaluation split.

tasks.text: Freeze the current F5 recipe and a meeting/speaker-disjoint evaluation subset before tuning.
tasks.evidence: Twenty reviewed question IDs are frozen across six new meetings, disjoint from the five earlier audio-development meetings and their participants. Source and human reliability checks remain separate tasks.

tasks.text: Finish the missing spoken Assistant cue and question audio.
tasks.evidence: All 105 distinct questions have representative recordings beginning with Assistant. All 129 current text records include the cue. Eleven new questions use separately authorized later same-speaker enrollment only for offline TTS; the frozen twenty-question subset uses earlier conditioning speech throughout. Automatic transcription disagreements remain visible for review.

tasks.text: Review the frozen subset for who committed to what, revised plans and constraints spread across speakers.
tasks.evidence: Use short verified fact checklists for scoring, with uncertainty retained. Reference-answer audio remains deferred.

tasks.text: Include ordinary discussion where the assistant should stay silent.
tasks.evidence: Store these as explicit non-request controls, rather than inventing a question at every point.

tasks.text: Obtain independent naturalness, requester-motivation and voice/acoustic review of the frozen examples.

stages.title: 2. Establish whether available history supports correct answers
stages.goal: Compare full ground-truth transcript history, recent history and history without speaker labels; source evidence determines correctness.

tasks.text: Use the stronger Qwen3-30B Instruct reader for the newer transcript diagnostics.
tasks.evidence: The earlier 4B reader made ownership and plan-revision errors; the 30B reader also makes source-binding errors. Model approval is not the scoring reference.

tasks.text: Run matched full-history, recent-history and no-speaker-label controls on the frozen evaluation set.
tasks.evidence: Earlier studies contain some of these comparisons, but they do not constitute a complete matched evaluation of the new frozen subset.

tasks.text: Maintain an explicit meeting state with speaker, fact or commitment, decision status, evidence and source time.
tasks.evidence: Track proposed, agreed and superseded items separately so an older proposal cannot silently replace a later decision.

tasks.text: Curate earlier teacher traces before using them as training targets.
tasks.evidence: Reject fabricated quotations and stale facts. Verify copied evidence and updates against the history available at that time.

stages.title: 3. Run the original three audio questions through a controlled comparison
stages.goal: Compare S1 alone, reactive S2 with oracle history, reactive S2 with causal ASR history and background preparation with that same ASR history.

tasks.text: Qualify history retention before attempting the full 18–35-minute prefixes.
tasks.evidence: Short listening clips do not demonstrate long-context retention. Start with bounded histories and verify that earlier facts remain accessible as more conversation arrives.

tasks.text: Run the original three synthesized questions under all four conditions.
tasks.evidence: These three question events already have reviewed audio. The four-condition AMI system comparison has not been run.

tasks.text: Keep future question text and scoring checklists hidden from background preparation until the request arrives.
Count the entire pre-request cost, including preparation that becomes stale, is cancelled or is never useful.
tasks.evidence: Include input processing, reasoning and retained state. Do not charge only for preparation that later helps.

tasks.text: Measure correct answer facts and attribution together with response latency, listening deadlines and compute.
tasks.evidence: Use the same causal ASR history in the reactive and background conditions so extra future information cannot explain a gain.

stages.title: 4. Add tool use and learn when to act
stages.goal: Start with one sandboxed lookup with deterministic results, then evaluate heuristic action choices before supervised policy training.

tasks.text: Keep the existing scripted search/open examples as backend fixtures.
tasks.evidence: The earnings-call examples verify document lookup and availability gates. Codex supplied the queries and page choices; no model tool policy was demonstrated.

tasks.text: Add one controlled sandbox lookup task with deterministic results.
Include a case where later speech changes the request while lookup or preparation is pending.
Separate internal preparation from outward intervention with explicit actions: listen, prepare, answer/clarify, call a tool, cancel/revise.
Establish heuristic baselines over those actions before training a supervised policy.
Use earnings calls and their associated documents as an extension after checking audio timing, source availability and reporting-period bindings.

resource_note: Audio completion uses the frozen F5 model on up to two L40S 48 GB GPUs, one per synthesis job; F5 and Vocos share GPU 0 in each job. ASR and speaker checks follow on one GPU. No S1/S2 comparison or policy training is part of this data-completion work.
update_rule: Update stage status only when the stated evidence exists. A larger corpus, completed synthesis or parsed model response does not mark the controlled system evaluation complete.
